title: SQL Injection - Authentication Bypass via Login Form
impact: An attacker can bypass authentication entirely and log in as any user including the administrator without knowing the password by manipulating the SQL query's logic through unsanitized input in the email field.
remediation: Use parameterized queries/prepared statements instead of concatenating user input directly into SQL strings so injected SQL syntax cannot alter the query's logic.

title: SQL Injection — Data Extraction via Product Search (UNION-based)
impact: An unauthenticated attacker can extract arbitrary data from any table in the database including user emails and password hashes through the public product search endpoint by closing out the intended query and appending a UNION query so it can query tables outside its intended scope.
remediation: Use parameterized queries for product search and never include database credentials or password hashes in application responses.

title: Reflected XSS via Product Search Query
impact: An attacker can craft a malicious link containing script payload that executes in a victim's browser when the search query is reflected into the page.
remediation: Apply context-aware output encoding and validate or reject dangerous values in the search query before rendering them in HTML.

title: Stored XSS via User Registration
impact: An attacker can register an account using a malicious HTML payload that gets stored in the application. When an administrator views the Registered Users section of the Administration page, the payload executes JavaScript in the administrator's browser, potentially allowing further client-side attacks within the victim's session.
remediation: Apply context-aware output encoding when displaying user-supplied data. Sanitize HTML inputs where necessary and implement a Content Security Policy (CSP) as an additional layer of protection.
